title: GUI-Enhance FSM
description: Guides generation and gives validation something to check against. Describes WHAT must be true of the environment -- which input is reached through which interaction -- never HOW to build it. No selectors, no DOM structure, no component or framework choices; those belong to the coding agent, and constraining them is what makes environments look alike.

candidate.description: False when the task's input does not belong in an interface at all -- a bundled source tree to repair, say. Then `reason` is the whole document and nothing else is required.

reason.description: Required when candidate is false: what about this task's input makes an interface the wrong container for it.

domain.description: e.g. Developer Tools, Financial ERP, Observability

app_concept.description: One line: what the app pretends to be.

signature_vars.description: Page signature sigma: the controllable configuration carried across states.

visible_data.description: Prose, and a two-sided contract: what is legible to someone standing in this state, and by omission what this surface must never reveal. A value legible before the action meant to earn it makes that action decorative.

description.description: Semantic intent, e.g. 'apply the branch facet'. NOT an implementation instruction.

precondition.description: Boolean constraint over signature_vars; empty means always available.

data_placement.description: Where each staged input file ends up. Every file under input/ must appear exactly once. Not everything belongs in the interface -- a schema contract or a bundled repository is more honestly left on disk -- so a file left alone is a decision, recorded as such, not an omission.

source.description: Path relative to input/, exactly as staged. May carry a fragment naming a part of the file, e.g. 'records.json#/records'.

disposition.description: 'gui': obtainable only through the interface. 'file': stays on disk as it is.

reason.description: Required for 'file': why this one is better left alone.

split.description: For 'gui': how the content divides across the interface. Free-form -- whole on one surface, one piece per detail page, grouped into sections, revealed only under a filter, or something the shape of this particular file suggests.

modality.description: For 'gui': what interaction earns it. Free-form, and mixing several across one environment is encouraged. Examples, not a menu: rendered text, a downloaded export, a value that only appears on hover, a section that starts collapsed, results that exist only after a form is submitted, a figure legible from a chart, content split across two applications, a record reachable only by sorting or paging to it.

state.description: For 'gui': the state in which it becomes legible.

path.description: For 'gui': action ids from the initial state.

repeat_per_piece.description: True when the path must be walked once per piece rather than yielding everything at once.

min_actions.description: Lower bound: below it the environment poses no real work.

max_actions.description: Upper bound: above it the environment tests patience rather than capability.

noise_plan.description: UI chrome only -- never carries input, so it cannot threaten correctness.
